info.name: cerebro
info.description:
Generated from the services' OpenAPI documents by scripts/generate_postman.py -- do not edit by hand.

1. Set `baseUrl` (the gateway, default http://localhost:8080).
2. Set `token` to an API token, or run Auth > Sign in with password to fetch a session token.
Every service lives under {{baseUrl}}/api/<service>.

request.description:
Per-day counts of memories created and of memories edited on a later day
(`updated_at` on a different UTC day than `created_at`), for the last `days`
days or for the calendar `year`, plus the years that have any visible
activity. Days with no activity are omitted. Honors the token's context scope
and the ownership gate, like `/timeline`.

Hard-deletes a context. 409 if it still has memories (of any status),
unless `?force=true` - in which case those memories (and, via cascade, their
`memory_edges`) are hard-deleted first. `admin`-only (plan_v2.md SS9: token
management-adjacent, destructive), regardless of `write` scope.

Dumps the complete `disambiguation_log` (or only the resolved rows with
`resolved_only=true`) as {query, candidates, chosen_context, resolved_by,
created_at} -- the raw dataset that `cerebro-memory export-disambiguations`
(CLI) converts to JSONL for a future local fine-tuning (Phase 4,
plan_v2.md SS8). Does not filter by agent nor paginate: it's a full export,
meant to be run once there is real volume.

Portal-only (no client/MCP/CLI mirror): the `audit_log` (which agent did what), newest
first, keyset-paginated by id. Admin only: search queries are in there.

Paginated browse of memories (no semantic ranking -- that is `/memories/search`),
newest first by default. Filters: `context` (slug), `type`, `status` (default
`active`; `all` for every status). Honors the token's context scope (a restricted
token asking for an out-of-scope `context` gets 403) and the ownership gate.

Hybrid retrieval. `scope` controls the Context Engine (plan_v2.md SS7):

- explicit `context=<slug>` (or `scope=<slug>` not equal to auto/all) filters
  directly, no engine involved - `scope_decision.mode == "explicit"`.
- `scope=all` (default off) is the Fase 1 behavior: unfiltered hybrid search
  across every context - kept for the benchmark's control arm.
- `scope=auto` (default) runs the Context Engine: a cheap deterministic
  preliminary scoring decides whether one context clearly dominates
  (`mode == "auto"`, results already filtered to it) or the query is
  ambiguous between 2-4 contexts (`mode == "ambiguous"`, `results` comes back
  empty on purpose - see `results_by_candidate` for a few results per
  candidate instead, and `disambiguation_id` to resolve the choice later via
  POST /disambiguations/{id}/resolve).

`expand` (Fase 3, default False): when True, adds a separate `related` block
with the 1-hop neighbors (memory_edges + the virtual supersedence chain) of
the top 3 `results`, deduplicated, capped at 5. `related` is NEVER merged into
`results` - it must not perturb retrieval metrics. Neighbors from a different
context than the one this search resolved to (if any) are included only when
reached via an explicit edge (`cross_context: true` on that entry) - explicit
edges are intentional user-made bridges, not contamination.

One memory by id, with the same context-scope and ownership checks as
`/memories/{id}/related`.

1-hop neighbors of `memory_id`, both directions, plus the derived
supersedence chain (`relation="supersedes"`) - see `graph.get_related`.

`allowed_contexts` (plan_v2.md SS9): 403 if `memory_id` itself sits in a
disallowed context (a missing memory still 404s normally, below - a
restricted token can't tell "forbidden" from "doesn't exist" from this check
alone). Neighbors from a disallowed context are dropped from `related`
entirely, even ones reached via an explicit edge - `cross_context` marks an
intentional bridge for tokens that CAN see both sides, it is not an allowlist
bypass for tokens that can't.

`episodic`/`decision` memories, ordered by effective date
(`occurred_at`, or `created_at` if there is no `occurred_at`) most recent first -
meant for "what happened in X over the last few weeks". Filters: `context` (slug),
`from`/`to` (effective date range), `limit` (default 50).

Per-day counts of documents created and of documents edited on a later
UTC day, for the last `days` days or for the calendar `year` (days without
activity are omitted), plus the years that have any visible activity.
Honors the token's category scope and the ownership gate.

`hidden=true` never shows up here (no parameter to turn it off -- see
luisjdev-pendientes/ecosistema-cerebro): a hidden category is only
reachable by knowing its exact slug in advance (create_document/get_document
don't filter by `hidden`, only this listing does).

Renames/edits a category WITHOUT touching `documents` - its documents'
`/{category}/{slug}` routes change for free when the join resolves,
because `category_id` is an FK, never copied text (ecosistema-cerebro.md
SS6). If the slug changes, registers a redirect for each document in the
category (its external route moves even though `category_id` doesn't change) - see
luisjdev-pendientes/ecosistema-cerebro, "Slug redirects".

409 if the category still has documents, unless `?force=true` - in which
case `documents.category_id`'s `ON DELETE CASCADE` (and
`document_versions.document_id`'s over those documents) does the full
cascade with a single DELETE. `admin`-only, same criterion as
`DELETE /contexts/{slug}` in cerebro-memory (destructive).

Dedicated listing of archived documents (never mixed with
`GET /documents`) - see luisjdev-pendientes/ecosistema-cerebro, "Archiving".

Paginated browse for the portal's table (active, archived or both, sortable, with
a total). Same visibility rules as `GET /documents`: an explicit `category` is taken
as-is, otherwise `hidden` categories are left out and `allowed_categories` applies;
`owner_filter` stacks on top. `q` is full-text and, when given, orders by relevance.
Only the portal consumes it, so it has no client/MCP/CLI mirror.

Exact route: works the same for archived documents and for `hidden`
categories (neither is filtered here, only in listings) -- but it DOES
respect `principal.owner_filter` (a separate, additional gate from the
category one): reading a document by its exact known path must not bypass
ownership. If there's no direct match, falls back to `slug_redirects` --
the real document at its current route ALWAYS wins over a redirect; the
fallback only runs when the direct lookup already returned a 404 (see
luisjdev-pendientes/ecosistema-cerebro) -- and a redirected document must
ALSO pass the ownership check before being returned.

Full replacement (includes moving categories). Mandatory transactionality
(ecosistema-cerebro.md SS12): `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` of the row,
INSERT of the prior snapshot into `document_versions`, and the `UPDATE`, all in ONE
single transaction - content is never read in a separate query without a lock.

Partial patch by heading (ecosistema-cerebro.md SS12): section = from the
heading to the next one at the same level or higher. Same mandatory
transactionality as `replace_document` - `FOR UPDATE` + snapshot + UPDATE in one
single transaction.

Registered BEFORE `GET /documents/{category}/{slug}` on purpose: both
routes have 2 segments after `/documents/`, and this one must win over that
(more generic) one so `/documents/<uuid>/versions` doesn't get interpreted as
category='<uuid>', slug='versions'. Read-only -- no restore endpoint,
see luisjdev-pendientes/ecosistema-cerebro, "document_versions with no
way to read it".

Counts of categories/documents/versions (minimal mirror of cerebro-memory's
GET /stats). With `allowed_categories` restricted, counts only what's visible
to that token -- same silent-filtering criterion as the rest of cerebro-docs'
listings (never a 403 on an aggregate, it's just narrowed).

Per-day counts of flow definitions created (`created`) and runs started
(`updated`), for the last `days` days or for the calendar `year` (days without
activity are omitted), plus the years that have any visible activity. Honors
the token's category scope and the ownership gate on definitions.
Edits a category's name/description (portal-only, no client/MCP/CLI mirror).

409 while the category still has flows, unless `?force=true`: the FKs' ON DELETE
CASCADE then remove its flows, their versions and their runs. `admin`-only, like
deleting a docs category or a memory context (destructive).
Mermaid flowchart of the COMPLETE definition (for people; execution still reveals one step at a time).
cerebro-docs URIs the current definition points at (metadata references and delegate prompts).
Every saved version of the definition, newest first.

Portal-only (no client/MCP/CLI mirror): every run event across all flows (`flow_run_events`),
newest first (insertion order), keyset-paginated by `seq`. Admin only.

Runs of the flows the caller can see. `awaiting=true` keeps only in-progress runs
stopped at a checkpoint nobody approved (the approval queue); that position lives in
Redis, so that mode is filtered in memory (capped to the 1000 most recent in-progress runs).
The run's audit trail, oldest first (`flow_run_events`).
Portal-only: every group with its members and the modules/scopes it grants.
Memberships and the group's scopes go with it (FK cascade); the users stay.

Username + password login. Returns a session token that expires after
`session_ttl_hours`. Any failure (unknown user, wrong password, revoked
user, user with no password) answers the same 401; a locked account
answers 429 with `Retry-After`.

Revoke the session token used for this request. Only session tokens
(minted by a password login) can be logged out; any other token is
revoked by name with `DELETE /tokens/{name}`.

Portal-only (no client/MCP/CLI mirror): switch a token off (`disabled_at = now()`) or back
on (`disabled_at = NULL`); the secret never changes. Different from revoking, which is
permanent: a revoked token cannot be switched (409).

Portal-only (no client/MCP/CLI mirror). Refuses to leave the system without an
active admin: demoting or deactivating the last one is a 409.

Set a user's password. An admin may set anyone's. A non-admin may only
change their own, and must prove the current one (which counts toward the
same lockout as a login). Every session of the user is closed.
